the hypocretin peptide system is expressed early in development, is functional early in development, and may play a role in the early regulation of sleep and feeding.

the expression of the hypocretins and receptors occurs very early during development and the hypocretin‐induced excitatory influence on LH neuronal activity is robust and occurs early during development.

the hypocretin peptide and receptor systems are strongly expressed early during development, and that both the peptide and the receptors have a potent excitatory effect on the activity of neurons in the lateral and posterior hypothalamus.

the developmental expression of the hypocretins and their receptors, and the functional effects of these peptides on neuronal activity in the developing lateral hypothalamus.
the role of hypocretin in the regulation of sleep/wakefulness and energy balance, and the developmental profile of this system.
the developmental profile of a recently discovered neuropeptide, hypocretin.

the LH is a major site of hypocretin synthesis and that hypocretin exes a profound excitatory effect on LH cells early in development.

the LH is a critical brain region for development of arousal and survival, that it contains the earliest known source of hypocretin in the brain, and that the LH is the earliest site of hypocretin action in the brain, which is likely to contribute to the development and regulation of arousal, feeding, and other functions.

the hypocretin‐containing neurons are activated early during development and are involved in the regulation of the development of the central nervous system.

the development of the hypocretins and their receptors is a critical step in the development of the brain and that the early expression of the hypocretine system is a key factor in the development of independent feeding behavior, arousal, and sleep regulation.

the orexin (hypocretin) system is already functional early in development and that it is likely to play an important role in the early development of sleep/wake and arousal states.
